tagline: Sandbars, bluffs, and a river left to run.
intro: The Lower Wisconsin River Road follows the last free-flowing stretch of the Wisconsin River, from Sauk Prairie toward its meeting with the Mississippi. There are no dams on this stretch, and much of the riverbank is protected as the Lower Wisconsin State Riverway.
The road stays close to the valley, crossing farm country and small towns between wooded bluffs.
season: Summer for sandbar picnics and paddling, autumn for the bluffs.

moments.title: Sauk Prairie
moments.text: The twin towns of Sauk City and Prairie du Sac sit where the river leaves its last dam.

moments.title: Spring Green
moments.text: A river town known for its theatre and its architecture, a short drive off the byway.

moments.title: Riverway sandbars
moments.text: The river's sandbars are a paddling destination rather than a roadside stop. Plan a separate outing.

moments.title: Wyalusing State Park
moments.text: High bluffs overlook the confluence of the Wisconsin and Mississippi rivers.
